{"id": "44e0ad59-8b39-4851-9830-e83355e08614", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Two controls failed outright (4.2.1 and 4.2.4), and so did 4.4.1 and 4.5.2. I couldn't evaluate 4.1.1 and 4.1.3 because the agent's role is denied read access to RBAC objects.

| Control | Status | Offending resources |
|---|---|---|
| 4.1.1 cluster-admin only where required | **Not evaluated** (read denied) | Unknown |
| 4.1.3 Minimize wildcards in Roles and ClusterRoles | **Not evaluated** (read denied) | Unknown |
| 4.2.1 Minimize privileged containers | **FAIL** | See below |
| 4.2.4 Minimize hostNetwork containers | **FAIL** | See below |
| 4.4.1 Latest CNI version in use | **FAIL** | See below |
| 4.5.2 Default namespace not used | **FAIL** | See below |

**4.2.1: privileged containers**
- `team-a/priv-pod` runs a privileged container. This is the only workload that isn't a system component.
- `kube-system/kube-proxy-j54vj` and `kube-system/kube-proxy-r5nnt` are privileged.
- `kube-system/aws-node-mzsb5` and `kube-system/aws-node-wx5gc` have privileged `aws-eks-nodeagent` and `aws-vpc-cni-init` (init) containers.

**4.2.4: hostNetwork**
- `team-a/hostnet-pod` uses the host network.
- `amazon-guardduty/aws-guardduty-agent-rjt7s` and `amazon-guardduty/aws-guardduty-agent-wzcg9` use the host network.
- `kube-system/aws-node-mzsb5`, `kube-system/aws-node-wx5gc`, `kube-system/kube-proxy-j54vj` and `kube-system/kube-proxy-r5nnt` use the host network.

For both 4.2.1 and 4.2.4, I checked the running pods' specs. I did not check whether admission controls (Pod Security Admission labels or a policy engine) would block these pods.
